kjv: have laid a wound under thee (Edom)
mine: have set a trap beneath you (Edom)
note: mazor here is usually derived from a root "net/snare" (or emended mazor = "trap"); "wound" (mazor elsewhere) makes little sense "under" someone.

kjv: thou (Edom) shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger
mine: do not gloat over the day of your (Edom's) brother in the day of his misfortune
note: al-tere with jussive forms is a prohibition (warning or retrospective rebuke); nokhro is "his misfortune/disaster", not "became a stranger".
